name: Atlantic North Equatorial Countercurrent
scope: Declared 42 W to 32 W western summer study reach: one editor-selected NECC connection inside the source regional surface-flow context. Branch assignment and joining remain review gates. Excludes independent northern-branch geometry, upstream NBC retroflection, equatorial ESC and eastern-basin continuation. Not a whole-current length or sum of branches. All latitude gates and bends are editorial.
layer: Altimetry-derived surface geostrophic context; no fixed-depth velocity core, parcel trajectory or depth-uniform axis inferred.
time_convention: Editorial route guided by the 1993-2017 boreal-summer climatological context (July-August-September). Not a dated axis, monthly mean measured centerline or year-round route.
source_locator: Sections 2.1, 3 and 4.2 identify HS5 at 42 W and HS6 at 32 W; section 6 / Fig. 8 caption defines summer JAS. The explicit east-of-38-W branch joining description concerns fall, not a verified summer connection. All route latitudes and bends are editorial.
source_citation: Dimoune et al. (2023), Revisiting the tropical Atlantic western boundary circulation from a 25-year time series of satellite altimetry data, Ocean Science 19, 251-268, doi:10.5194/os-19-251-2023.
source_license: Open-access source, CC BY 4.0; facts paraphrased with attribution. No source images or velocity arrays packaged.
coordinate_selection: Source section longitudes bound the reach. OSW selects nominal gates 42 W 6 N and 32 W 6.5 N and intermediate 38 W 6.2 N, 35 W 6.4 N. No figure digitization or field-derived axis; branch correspondence and interpolation require review.

alternative_routes.interpretation: Editorial bend sensitivity, not season or edge.

scenario_rule: Three declared shapes crossed with uniform longitude offsets -0.25/0/+0.25 and independent endpoint-latitude offsets -0.25/0/+0.25 degrees: 81 editorial cases, not width bounds, seasonal extrema or confidence intervals.
remaining_gates: Review chosen latitude gates and interpolation against compatible summer velocity fields.
